title: Penguin Body Size in R
text:
How do average body mass and flipper length differ by penguin species and sex?
Data: Palmer Penguins, collected by Kristen Gorman and Palmer Station Antarctica LTER. The data are available under the CC0 licence.
Citation: Horst, A. M., Hill, A. P., & Gorman, K. B. (2020). palmerpenguins: Palmer Archipelago (Antarctica) penguin data. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3960218.
library(palmerpenguins)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

title: Penguin Body Size in R
text:
Check the data

penguins <- palmerpenguins::penguins
columns <- c("species", "sex", "body_mass_g", "flipper_length_mm")

print(paste("Number of penguins:", nrow(penguins)))

[1] "Number of penguins: 344"

print("Missing values in the columns I will use:")

[1] "Missing values in the columns I will use:"

print(colSums(is.na(penguins[columns])))

          species               sex       body_mass_g flipper_length_mm 
                0                11                 2                 2 


Some rows are missing a measurement or a sex value. I check these before comparing groups.

title: Penguin Body Size in R
text:
Remove incomplete rows

clean <- penguins[complete.cases(penguins[columns]), ]

print(paste("Rows kept:", nrow(clean)))

[1] "Rows kept: 333"

print(paste("Rows removed:", nrow(penguins) - nrow(clean)))

[1] "Rows removed: 11"

print(head(clean[columns]))

# A tibble: 6 × 4
  species sex    body_mass_g flipper_length_mm
  <fct>   <fct>        <int>             <int>
1 Adelie  male          3750               181
2 Adelie  female        3800               186
3 Adelie  female        3250               195
4 Adelie  female        3450               193
5 Adelie  male          3650               190
6 Adelie  female        3625               181


I use the same complete rows for the summary and plot.

title: Penguin Body Size in R
text:
Calculate group averages

summary <- clean |>
  group_by(species, sex) |>
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean_mass_g = mean(body_mass_g),
    mean_flipper_mm = mean(flipper_length_mm),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(as.data.frame(summary), row.names = FALSE)

   species    sex count mean_mass_g mean_flipper_mm
    Adelie female    73    3368.836        187.7945
    Adelie   male    73    4043.493        192.4110
 Chinstrap female    34    3527.206        191.7353
 Chinstrap   male    34    3938.971        199.9118
    Gentoo female    58    4679.741        212.7069
    Gentoo   male    61    5484.836        221.5410


Gentoo males have the highest average body mass of 5484.8 g, while Adelie females have the lowest average body mass of 3368.8 g. Within each species, males have a higher average body mass than females.
Gentoo males have the longest average flipper length of 221.5 mm, while Adelie females have the shortest of 187.8 mm. Within each species, similarly, males have longer average flipper lengths than females.

title: Penguin Body Size in R
text:
Plot average body mass

ggplot(summary, aes(x = species, y = mean_mass_g, fill = sex)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    x = "Species",
    y = "Average body mass (g)",
    fill = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()







Figure 1: Average body mass by penguin species and sex.





The plot here shows the average body mass by penguin species and sex. We can see that Gentoo penguins have the highest average body mass in this sample.

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
My first week of MDS has definitely been a busy one. There has been a lot of adjustment compared with the first week of my undergraduate degree. The emails leading up to the program and orientation really emphasized how intensive MDS would be, but it was still jarring to experience it firsthand. The first week of classes has been great so far, and the program has many professors who genuinely want students to succeed. I have also made many new friends who come from diverse backgrounds and have very different experiences from me, which I think will bring a lot of unique perspectives to the program. I’m looking forward to getting to know everyone better.
Although it was expected, the biggest surprise so far has been the pace. In undergrad, I was used to having a week to settle into the course load and then working at a relatively comfortable pace for the rest of the term. In MDS, the pace picks up right from the start. There is a lot of material covered every day and many submissions due each week. If you miss anything, whether it is a lecture or a lab, the work can pile up quickly. Another thing that surprised me is how often we context switch. One lecture we might be learning Python for data science, and the next we are diving into R or statistics.
So far, I am enjoying the program as I get used to the intense schedule and fast-paced environment. I am also looking forward to creating new projects, learning new skills, and getting to know everyone better.

title: Penguin Body Size in Python
text:
How do average body mass and flipper length differ by penguin species and sex?
Data: Palmer Penguins, collected by Kristen Gorman and Palmer Station Antarctica LTER. The data are available under the CC0 licence.
Citation: Horst, A. M., Hill, A. P., & Gorman, K. B. (2020). palmerpenguins: Palmer Archipelago (Antarctica) penguin data. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3960218.

title: Penguin Body Size in Python
text:
Check the data

from palmerpenguins import load_penguins
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

penguins = load_penguins()
columns = ["species", "sex", "body_mass_g", "flipper_length_mm"]

print("Number of penguins:", len(penguins))
print("Missing values in the columns I will use:")
print(penguins[columns].isna().sum())

Number of penguins: 344
Missing values in the columns I will use:
species               0
sex                  11
body_mass_g           2
flipper_length_mm     2
dtype: int64


Some rows are missing a measurement or a sex value. I check these before comparing groups.

title: Penguin Body Size in Python
text:
Remove incomplete rows

clean = penguins.dropna(subset=columns).copy()

print("Rows kept:", len(clean))
print("Rows removed:", len(penguins) - len(clean))
print(clean[columns].head())

Rows kept: 333
Rows removed: 11
  species     sex  body_mass_g  flipper_length_mm
0  Adelie    male       3750.0              181.0
1  Adelie  female       3800.0              186.0
2  Adelie  female       3250.0              195.0
4  Adelie  female       3450.0              193.0
5  Adelie    male       3650.0              190.0


I use the same complete rows for the summary and plot.

title: Penguin Body Size in Python
text:
Calculate group averages

summary = (
    clean.groupby(["species", "sex"], as_index=False)
    .agg(
        count=("body_mass_g", "size"),
        mean_mass_g=("body_mass_g", "mean"),
        mean_flipper_mm=("flipper_length_mm", "mean"),
    )
)

print(summary.round(1).to_string(index=False))

  species    sex  count  mean_mass_g  mean_flipper_mm
   Adelie female     73       3368.8            187.8
   Adelie   male     73       4043.5            192.4
Chinstrap female     34       3527.2            191.7
Chinstrap   male     34       3939.0            199.9
   Gentoo female     58       4679.7            212.7
   Gentoo   male     61       5484.8            221.5


Gentoo males have the highest average body mass of 5484.8 g, while Adelie females have the lowest average body mass of 3368.8 g. Within each species, males have a higher average body mass than females.
Gentoo males have the longest average flipper length of 221.5 mm, while Adelie females have the shortest of 187.8 mm. Within each species, similarly, males have longer average flipper lengths than females.

title: Penguin Body Size in Python
text:
Plot average body mass

mass_by_group = summary.pivot(
    index="species",
    columns="sex",
    values="mean_mass_g",
)

ax = mass_by_group.plot.bar()
ax.set_xlabel("Species")
ax.set_ylabel("Average body mass (g)")
ax.legend(title="Sex")
plt.xticks(rotation=0)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()







Figure 1: Average body mass by penguin species and sex.





The plot here shows the average body mass by penguin species and sex. We can see that Gentoo penguins have the highest average body mass in this sample.

title: About
text:
I grew up in the Lower Mainland and did my undergraduate degree in Mathematics and Computing Science at Simon Fraser University. During my time at SFU, I worked on a project with the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority, where my team and I submitted a paper to the Canadian Operational Research Society on using an LSTM machine learning model to predict cargo throughput six weeks in advance.
I also completed a co-op with Fraser Health Authority, where I worked on integration pipelines that processed thousands of messages a day across different healthcare systems.
More recently, I founded Planarize, an AI takeoff and quoting platform built for window and door companies. We reduce the time it takes to create a quote from hours to seconds.
